examples.label: Package it into a deployable WAR

notes: Deploying a WAR through /manager/html requires manager-script or manager-gui role. The app path equals the WAR name, so backup.war is reached at /backup/.

recommended.note: Provides the manager creds to deploy the WAR.
Upgrade the JSP webshell to a reverse shell.

name: Tomcat - JSP WAR Webshell Deploy
command: zip -r backup.war cmd.jsp   # then deploy via /manager and run
description: Packages a JSP command-shell into a WAR, deploys it through the authenticated Manager app, and executes commands via the deployed endpoint.

defense.why_it_works: Tomcat's Manager application accepts WAR uploads and deploys them automatically. A WAR containing a JSP webshell is instantly accessible at /<war-name>/<file.jsp> executing commands via Runtime.exec() as the Tomcat process user.
defense.prerequisites: Valid manager-script or manager-gui credentials. /manager accessible from the attacker.
defense.impact: Persistent JSP webshell running as the Tomcat OS user. Enables file read/write, lateral movement, and reverse shell upgrade.
defense.detection: WAR deployment via POST to /manager/deploy. New application context in Tomcat. GET requests to new JSP with cmd parameter. Unusual child processes spawned by Tomcat.
defense.artifacts: Tomcat manager access log (POST /manager/deploy) | catalina.out: new context deployed | Web server log (GET /backup/cmd.jsp?cmd=id) | Process audit log (bash spawned from java)
defense.prevention: Restrict /manager to localhost. Use manager-script role only. Monitor WAR deployments. Run Tomcat as a low-privilege user. Use AppArmor/SELinux to restrict Tomcat process capabilities.
defense.misconfiguration: Tomcat Manager accessible from internet. manager-gui role assigned. Tomcat runs as root or has excessive filesystem privileges.
defense.vulnerable_config:
<!-- Tomcat -- manager reachable from any IP, weak auth, runs as root -->
<!-- conf/context.xml -- no IP restriction -->
<!-- Valve for RemoteAddrValve commented out -->

<!-- conf/tomcat-users.xml -->
<role rolename="manager-gui"/>
<role rolename="manager-script"/>
<user username="admin" password="admin" roles="manager-gui,manager-script"/>

<!-- systemd/init -- Tomcat running as root -->
# /etc/systemd/system/tomcat.service
[Service]
User=root
ExecStart=/opt/tomcat/bin/startup.sh
defense.secure_config:
<!-- Tomcat -- restrict manager, strong auth, run as dedicated user -->
<!-- conf/context.xml -->
<Context>
  <Valve className="org.apache.catalina.valves.RemoteAddrValve"
         allow="127\.0\.0\.1|::1"/>
</Context>

<!-- conf/tomcat-users.xml -->
<role rolename="manager-script"/>
<user username="deploy" password="Rnd0mStr0ng!Pass#9" roles="manager-script"/>
<!-- Remove manager-gui role entirely in production -->

<!-- /etc/systemd/system/tomcat.service -->
[Service]
User=tomcat
Group=tomcat
ExecStart=/opt/tomcat/bin/startup.sh
defense.evasion: Use manager-script REST API (/manager/text/deploy) instead of GUI upload to avoid form-based WAF triggers.
